Why Duncanville businesses miss calls

Duncanville sits along I-20 in south Dallas County, and over a third of residents speak Spanish at home. Food and hospitality employ about 10% of workers, and transportation and utilities over 9%. Many homes are decades old and need regular repairs, and many customers work shifts or commute. A small plumbing or auto shop can take a Spanish call and an English call back to back while its only tech is on a job.

Can you keep your Duncanville phone number?

Yes. Duncanville callers will usually see the 214, 469, 972 and 945 area codes, and you can keep the number customers already know. Forward it to the AI for all calls, only after hours, or only when your team does not pick up. We can also set up a new local number. Everything is set up remotely, so you do not need new equipment or a visit to an office.

What to check before you go live

  1. Test real calls: ask awkward questions, not only easy ones, and listen to how it handles them.
  2. Set the rules: decide which calls transfer to a person and which become messages.
  3. Plan your minutes: estimate your busiest month, not an average one.
  4. Tell callers what you need to: Texas is generally treated as a one-party consent state for recording calls, but rules differ for callers in other states, so check with your advisor if you record calls.
